On Boxing Day whilst we were holding our usual holiday meeting in Battersea Park we were represented in the Surrey Walking Club Croydon to Godstone and back walk by what was described elsewhere as a C3 team That however was a libel on R D McMullen, E.

McMullen finished third with Jack Rutland fourth. In the Field Events several new title holders were seen, and Alan Dunn is to be complimented on bringing off a fine double in winning the Javelin and Discus events.
Harry Churcher won the London Business Houses 7 miles Walking Championship on January 8th, at Southgate, and R.

With two in the first positions, James and East well up in support, the team race was as good as won by the Bels. but a keen fight was going on for the second place between Highgate and Surrey W.C. with odds on the superior packing of Surrey to put them in front. This proved to be the case and after…
Gregory, was an absentee, as also was Harry Churcher and R. McMullen, and the new title-holder proved to be J.
Denis Merrett was 2nd in the 220 yds. final, and Ian Badiali was 3rd in the 880 yds. R. McMullen was 3rd in the 2 mile walk and Dennis Fleming was placed 3rd in the Javelin Throw.
In the 2 miles walk we saw R. McMullen lead the field home from Gerry Warr and Ted Smith, and in the match against Surrey W.C. we won with 89 to 126 pts.
R. McMullen won the 2 miles Walk, after a long string of second places, and his time of 15 mins. 5.4 secs. was quite good after his lay-off during the winter season.
The handicap was won by one of our up and coming lads, Bob Phillips, with that improving youngster Ray Middleton, 3rd and "Evergreen" Doub. splitting them for 2nd place. First man home was R.

Being the first open of the season we did not expect any very startling result and our "A" team finished 4th. R. McMullen was our first man home in 56.11, with George Checkley 15th, Hugh McGreechan 17th and Eric Hall 23rd.
The Surrey 10 Miles Championship was held at Kingston and we congratulate R. McMullen on winning the individual title in 79.39 and the team on making the double.

With Eric Hall 4th, R.D.McMullen 16th and George Checkley 19th we easily won the team race from Met.W.C. and Highgate. It was very pleasing to see the large number of Club supporters stationed around the course - their presence was well rewarded.

Dave McMullen, by finishing second, gave a good indication of his ability over this distance and a newcomer to the distance, J.Keown put up a sterling performance, and with a little more experience should soon be among the top notchers.
